claims.text: A machine-learning-based interatomic potential can capture the complex interactions in multicomponent high-entropy alloys more accurately than TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The proposed potential would improve representation of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid.
Improved representation of atomic interactions and configurations would increase reference-target phase-space overlap.
Better reference-target phase-space overlap would reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed potential would reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch would be reduced by at least 20% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The reduction in path mismatch can be measured using the free-energy difference between the reference and target systems.
The intervention is applicable to high-entropy alloys containing 3-6 principal elements.
The intervention is applicable from 0.8 to 1.2 times the melting temperature.
The intervention applies to both solid and liquid states near their high melting temperatures.
The accuracy of the proposed potential may depend on the quality of its training data.
The accuracy of the proposed potential may depend on the complexity of interactions in the high-entropy alloy.
A reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch of less than 10% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references would falsify the hypothesis.
